case_title: OSPF Neighbor Down Due to Timer Mismatch
ai_root_cause: OSPF Process ID mismatch between Router R1 (Process 1) and Router R2 (Process 2) caused adjacency failure.
human_correction: OSPF Process IDs are locally significant on each router and do NOT need to match. The actual failure was caused by Hello/Dead timer mismatch (10s/40s on R1 vs 5s/20s on R2).
lesson_learned: LLMs can conflate local configuration parameters (Process IDs) with protocol negotiation requirements (Timers, Area IDs, MTU, Subnet Masks). Rule-based timer diffing protects against this hallucination.

ai_root_cause: The entire router interface G0/0 is broken; rewrite all access-lists and replace the core switch configuration.
human_correction: Sub-interface G0/0.10 simply lacked the command 'encapsulation dot1Q 10'. Only 2 CLI commands were needed on the sub-interface, not a destructive network reconfiguration.
lesson_learned: Generative models may propose overly broad or destructive reconfiguration when a surgical 1-line command is sufficient. Network engineers must verify scope of changes.

case_title: DHCP APIPA Address on Multi-Subnet Campus
ai_root_cause: DHCP server service is offline or crashed because the host received a 169.254.x.x link-local address.
human_correction: The DHCP server was online on subnet 10.1.1.0/24; the client was on subnet 192.168.20.0/24. The default gateway router interface G0/1 was missing 'ip helper-address 10.1.1.100' to relay broadcast DISCOVER packets across layer 3.
lesson_learned: AI diagnoses can jump to single-subnet assumptions when diagnosing broadcast protocols across routed boundaries. The system must verify helper-address presence.

ai_root_cause: Public DNS resolution failure at Layer 7 prevents hosts from opening web pages.
human_correction: Root cause is Layer 3/4 NAT table exhaustion. The command 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface G0/0' omitted the keyword 'overload', restricting translation to a single concurrent host.
lesson_learned: Symptoms of packet drop at edge routers can mimic application or DNS failures if translation table state isn't examined. Check Layer 3/4 NAT translations first.

ai_root_cause: Remove the security access list completely using 'no ip access-group 100 in' on interface G0/0.
human_correction: Removing the entire ACL creates a critical security vulnerability by exposing the internal network. The correct fix is to insert 'permit tcp any host 10.0.0.10 eq 80' into ACL 100.
lesson_learned: AI recommendations may trade security for convenience by disabling firewalls/ACLs rather than tuning specific access control entries (ACEs).
